rules_text:
Rules summary For tips on how to play patchwork, see Tips_patchwork Setup Each player takes a 9×9 quilt board and 5 buttons as currency. The time tokens are put at the start of the board. Special patches are also placed. Place the regular patches in a circle. The neutral pawn starts after the 1×2 patch. Game play The player whose time token is behind takes the next turn. If they are on the same space, the player whose token is on top (the last one to arrive on that space) takes another turn. On your turn, you can either receive buttons or place patches. If you choose to receive buttons, move to the space one step further from your opponent. You receive 1 button for each space moved. If you choose to place patches, choose a patch at most three steps clockwise from the pawn and move the pawn to there. Pay buttons and advance time according to price, and place it on your quilt board. If while moving you pass a special patch, take it and place it on your quilt board. They are the only 1×1 patches. If you pass a button, you receive income. Take buttons equal to the number of buttons on your quilt board. If you are the first to have a 7×7 square on your quilt board, take the special tile. End of the Game The game ends when both players move to the last space. Any spaces beyond are forfeited. Each leftover button is worth 1 point. The special tile is worth 7 points. Each empty space on your quilt board is worth -2 points. The player with the most points wins. If it’s a tie, the player who moves to the last space first wins.

[Rating: 1/10] A lot of this designer's games have confusing rules. I also don't like it when games punish you with negative points for not being a good player when the game doesn't even give you enough turns.

[Rating: 1/10] 0/10 - 10th anniversary punchboards sucks. Joining this entry to the base game is a mistake  10/10 - Original is masterpiece though

[Rating: 1/10] Classic Uwe 2p take & make polyomino game, what still elevates this above other similar such games (including those by Uwe) is the associated economic costs of the tiles mattering just as much (if not more) than the shape of the tile itself which makes the "take" aspect every bit as interesting as the "make" half of the game. Big downside is that it's 2p only which gives it stiff competition for table time.

[Rating: 1.5/10] At the end of the day it's just another engine builder with matching amount of interaction (gentle queue cutting) and drowned in pedestrian brown pastels.   [i]Even with a potentially colourful theme, nope, you can't get clean bright colours, we'll drown them in brown so middle aged couples feel comfy around the game and somewhat sedated. Yes, I imagine sewing diagrams for kids and sewing magazines of old and they had white background (!) and clear colours. But somebody had to slap mimetic realism even on (basically) Tetris and this is why we can't have beautiful things. [/i]  Combining engine

[Rating: 2/10] Game mechanics are terrible, it's as if no one playtested this before.  Completely broken game.

[Rating: 2/10] So overhyped it's ridiculous. Can think of 20 much superior two player games I'd rather play.   Good filler for when you are really tired and do not want to think at all.  But then I would rather watch TV than play this. Decisions are simple and obvious.  Maybe it's good for fans of Tetris?  I am not a fan of Tetris.  Uwe has a hard time with his games. They are either overly complicated or incredibly simple. This is the mcdonald's of fillers. It's popularity is depressing.  I wish I had burned it instead of selling it.  That would have given me more satisfaction.

[Rating: 2/10] This game felt just too random for my taste and leaves me unsatisfied. I want to be able to strategize and some strategies might be possible but it's more of "let me try this and hope it works". The score is based on left over buttons which simply doesn't make sense. And there is no penalty for leaving holes inside your stitched patch versus leaving regions outside the patch un-stitched.
